newsitem.title: HONG KONG: KCRC says no plans to drop Jardine Fleming now.
newsitem.headline: KCRC says no plans to drop Jardine Fleming now.

text.p: The Kowloon-Canton Railway Corp (KCRC) said on Tuesday it does not at this stage intend to withdraw its portfolio from Jardine Fleming Investment Management.

Responding to earlier reports that it was assessing Jardine Fleming's future role in managing the company's pension fund, the Hong Kong railway utility said there were no plans afoot to remove its portfolio from Jardines.

"In response to a news report sent out this morning (October 8, 1996) by Reuters, the KCRC's general manager, human resources, Ms Esther Chan said that there was no intention for KCRC to withdraw its portfolio from Jardine Fleming at this stage," the company said in a news release.
Earlier on Tuesday, a company spokeswoman said the KCRC was assessing Jardine Fleming's continued management of its retirement funds following the regular quarterly review last September.

The Hong Kong Jockey Club's withdrawal of HK$1 billion from Jardine Fleming in the wake of a fund management trading scandal persuaded the KCRC to ask for an explanation during the regular quarterly review, the spokeswoman said.
"Following the case of the Hong Kong Jockey Club, we are now working with the benefit scheme consultants and our legal advisers to assess the situation," the spokeswoman said.
But the KCRC said the review referred to in the Reuters report referred to the regular quarterly review of the company's fund managers.

"The review mentioned in Reuters' report was a regular review conducted to KCRC's trustee to the retirement benefit scheme, held on a quarterly basis with every fund management firm under the scheme, in conjunction with the scheme's consultants and legal advisers," the company said.
Jardine Fleming is a joint venture between Robert Fleming of London and Hong Kong-based Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd .
